title: A Alibi for the Verdict Revisited
premise: True-crime podcaster Isandro Eriksen is hired by a wealthy stranger to prove that a woman declared dead thirty years ago — the only unsolved case in her archive — was never murdered at all. As Isandro digs, she realizes the 'victim' may have staged her death to escape a killer who has spent three decades erasing every trace of her survival, and that her client's payment was bait to draw out anyone still asking questions. When the killer surfaces and begins closing in on both the vanished woman and Isandro herself, she must stage one final broadcast as a trap. In the end, justice arrives outside any courtroom: the killer confesses on air, the woman chooses exile over vindication, and Isandro learns some cases close only by letting someone stay lost.
about_author: Petra Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent fifteen years transcribing testimony before turning to fiction. She writes cold-case mysteries from a farmhouse in rural Vermont, where she keeps a wall of unsolved files 'for inspiration.'

chapters.title: The Client Who Paid Too Much
chapters.summary: Isandro Eriksen receives an anonymous retainer — triple her usual fee — to prove that Marit Voss, dead since 1994, never existed as a victim at all. Through Isandro's POV, we see her pride and unease as she accepts. The emotional beat is seductive curiosity shadowed by instinct: no honest client pays this much for a negative.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Isandro reopens the Voss file, interviewing the retired detective who quit over it. His POV interlude reveals he always suspected the body wasn't Marit's — and that someone pressured him to stop looking. The beat is dread: the case isn't cold, it's frozen deliberately.

chapters.title: A Face That Wasn't Hers
chapters.summary: Forensic records show the 1994 dental evidence was falsified. Isandro, POV hers, tracks the now-dead dentist's assistant, who whispers that a man paid for the forgery — a man whose voice she'd know anywhere. Emotional beat: vertigo, as the alibi Isandro was hired to prove starts proving itself.

chapters.title: The Listener
chapters.summary: Isandro notices her podcast analytics: one listener downloads every episode within minutes of release, from rotating locations. Her producer's POV builds paranoia. Someone is monitoring her investigation in real time. Beat: the hunter realizes she is also prey.

chapters.title: What Survived
chapters.summary: A postmarked letter arrives containing a photograph of Marit alive, dated two years ago, with one line: 'Stop, or she finishes what he started.' Isandro, POV hers, realizes Marit is alive, hiding, and terrified of her rescuer as much as her pursuer. Beat: moral complication — saving Marit may destroy her.

chapters.title: The Man Who Knows the File
chapters.summary: The client finally reveals himself: Halvard Voss, Marit's brother, who has spent decades hunting the man who took her — or claims so. His POV chapter shows his intimate knowledge of the case file, matching the killer's profile exactly. Beat: chilling ambiguity about whether the client is savior or predator.

chapters.title: House of Borrowed Names
chapters.summary: Following the letter's trail, Isandro finds the coastal town where Marit lives under a false identity — and finds her neighbor recently dead under suspicious circumstances. Marit's own POV appears for the first time: exhausted, watchful, resigned. Beat: belonging bought at the price of everyone near you.

chapters.title: Confrontation at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Halvard arrives in town; Isandro realizes the timeline of the neighbor's death matches his movements. She confronts him on the tidal flats; he admits he found Marit years ago and has been 'protecting' her by eliminating witnesses. Beat: horror — the alibi was never for Marit; it was Halvard testing whether Isandro could be used against her.

chapters.title: The Last Broadcast
chapters.summary: Isandro stages a live episode claiming she's located Marit, forcing Halvard to act. With police tipped but unreliable, she traps his confession on air while Marit, choosing to stop running, steps out of hiding to face him. Climax: violence averted by exposure; the truth spoken aloud at last. Beat: terror transfigured into agency.

chapters.title: Verdict Without a Courtroom
chapters.summary: Halvard is arrested; Marit refuses to testify, vanishing again by choice. Isandro airs a final episode that closes the case without naming her, honoring the price of survival. Closing beat: bitterswet resolution — Isandro keeps her perfect record, but learns some clients pay not for answers, but for permission to disappear.
